children: Bank of Baroda (BoB) plans to scale up its subsidiaries to enhance their value to the parent bank and double their contribution to the Group’s overall profitability over the next two-three years.

The move is part of the public sector bank’s ambition to become a financial conglomerate, with the BoB Group seeking a presence across the entire para-banking spectrum, either directly or through its subsidiaries.

BoB has subsidiaries in areas such as credit cards, merchant banking and stock broking, back-office operations, IT services, mutual funds, life insurance and infrastructure debt financing. The group also includes The Nainital Bank Ltd.

“We primarily assess our subsidiaries’ contribution through their profitability and value to the Group’s valuation. Currently, they contribute around ₹200 crore per quarter, or roughly ₹800-1,000 crore annually, to the Group’s profitability. Considering the size of our bank and its position in the banking industry, this contribution is not yet significant enough,” Debadatta Chand, MD and CEO, told businessline.

India’s second-largest public sector bank, with total business of ₹32,57,883 crore, wants its subsidiaries to make a significantly larger contribution to the Group. However, it has not set specific long-term profit targets for individual subsidiaries.

“If a subsidiary is currently contributing ‘x’, we would ideally like to see that contribution increase to around ‘2x’ over the next two-three years. We have told these companies that capital will not be a constraint, but they must demonstrate the ability to grow and achieve meaningful scale. However, scaling up these businesses is not easy because these are finely priced, capital-intensive sectors,” Chand said.

The broader objective is to leverage BoB’s strength, brand and customer base across the parent bank and its subsidiaries, substantially increasing the latter’s contribution to consolidated profitability, he added.

The bank’s medium- to long-term strategy has two objectives: Enhancing value for the parent bank and building scale across its subsidiaries. “We have approached the Group strategy from two perspectives. First, we want to harness greater value from our existing subsidiaries. Second, we want to expand our presence in para-banking activities that the bank cannot efficiently undertake within its existing structure. We are not yet of a size where we can call ourselves a financial conglomerate.

“However, we want to establish a presence across the various activities that a large Indian or global bank typically undertakes. Merchant acquiring and payment businesses have become significant segments for private sector banks in India and globally. We want to participate in these emerging opportunities,” Chand said.
Last month, BoB Securities & Giltedge Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary, commenced operations as a non-deposit-taking NBFC, with the bank infusing an initial capital of ₹500 crore.

“Globally, large banks have strong treasury operations. While our treasury is already strong, its traditional role was primarily to manage reserve requirements. Over time, treasury operations have also become significant contributors through trading profits and other activities.

“However, if we want to tap opportunities in businesses such as debt capital markets, we may face certain limitations if we operate entirely within the bank. That is why we decided to establish a separate subsidiary,” Chand said.

The bank also sees significant opportunities in the domestic pension market. Towards this end, it has incorporated BoB Pension Fund Management Company Ltd, with an authorised share capital of ₹100 crore.

title: Eyeing financial conglomerate tag, plan to power up subsidiaries, says Bank of Baroda CEO
